paper_metadata.title: Compressive creep behavior of powder metallurgy manufactured Y2O3-reinforced TNM-B1 TiAl alloy with equiaxed and lamellar microstructure

evidence.quote: The high-temperature strength and compressive creep resistance of TNM B1-type TiAl alloy modified with Y2O3 nanoparticles are studied.

alloy_systems.name: TiAl-based alloy reinforced with Y2O3 nanoparticles

evidence.quote: The TNM-B1 alloy reinforced with Y2O3 nanoparticles has been produced by HEBM of elemental powder mixtures, followed by SHS and HIP of the milled synthesis products.

process_steps.method: high-energy ball milling (HEBM) and self-propagating high-temperature synthesis (SHS)

evidence.quote: Powder made of TNM-B1 alloy doped with 1 wt% Y2O3 nanoparticles (hereinafter, the notation “TNY” is used for this alloy) was employed as an initial material for preparing alloys. It was fabricated using HEBM + SHS.
HIP was conducted at 1250 °C and 145 MPa in an argon atmosphere. As shown below, the alloys produced in this mode have an equiaxed structure and are denoted as TNY-Eq.

process_steps.method: high-energy ball milling (HEBM) and self-propagating high-temperature synthesis (SHS)

evidence.quote: Powder made of TNM-B1 alloy doped with 1 wt% Y2O3 nanoparticles (hereinafter, the notation “TNY” is used for this alloy) was employed as an initial material for preparing alloys. It was fabricated using HEBM + SHS.
HIP was conducted at 1250 °C and 145 MPa in an argon atmosphere.

After HIP, some TNY alloy samples in hermetically sealed titanium capsules were subjected to heat treatment (HT) in an VSl-16-22-U vacuum furnace (Thermionic, Russia) at 1380 °C with a holding time of 2 h. This procedure aimed to form a lamellar microstructure in the alloy. The samples in this series are denoted as TNY-Lam.

Y2O3 nanoparticles made a significant contribution to the strengthening and creep resistance of the TNY-Eq alloy as they acted as an efficient barrier impeding dislocation motion and led to dislocation pile-up in the region adjacent to the nanoparticles
An analysis of electron diffraction recorded for this region revealed a high concentration of stacking faults as indicated by numerous extra reflections (Fig. 8a, inset).
